title: FCBoost: Static Frequency-Aware Channel Selection for 2-Bit KV Cache Quantization

contributions.purpose: Eliminate the per-page dynamic channel-selection overhead of mixed-precision 2-bit KV cache quantization.
contributions.mechanism: FCBoost: a static channel-selection method that profiles Contextual Agreement (CA) scores offline to identify structurally important RoPE frequency pairs, selects the top-F pairs per KV head to form a fixed boolean mask, then boosts those channels from INT2 to INT4 at inference.
contributions.evaluation: Reduces selection complexity from Kitty's O(N/P) to O(1) with no per-page metadata; short-context GSM8K sanity check 89.84% (within 0.46pp of FP16).
contributions.domain: LLM inference efficiency / KV cache quantization
contributions.source_quote: We introduce FCBoost, a static channel selection method that uses Contextual Agreement to identify RoPE frequency pairs requiring higher precision, eliminating per-page dynamic selection overhead.

contributions.purpose: Show the static frequency-aware mask beats dynamic magnitude-based boosting on accuracy.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate FCBoost vs Kitty (dynamic) and KIVI-KV2* (no boost) on AIME24/25 mathematical reasoning with Qwen3-8B at matched boost ratio (K=16 channels, F=8 pairs).
contributions.evaluation: FCBoost 71.11% average vs Kitty 66.67% (+4.44pp) and KIVI-KV2* 66.11% (+5.00pp), with much lower variance (std=1.57 vs 7-9).
contributions.domain: LLM inference efficiency / KV cache quantization
contributions.source_quote: On AIME24/25 benchmarks with Qwen3-8B, FCBoost achieves 71.11% average accuracy, outperforming Kitty by 4.44 percentage points while reducing selection complexity from O(N/P) to O(1).

contributions.purpose: Confirm that quantization sensitivity is structurally determined by RoPE frequency, not random or magnitude-based.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation comparing the CA-derived mask against random static masks (3 seeds), plus a CA-vs-magnitude channel-set overlap analysis.
contributions.evaluation: CA mask beats random masks by 6.67pp (71.11% vs 64.44%), and random masks fall below the no-boost baseline; CA vs magnitude sets have low Jaccard overlap (0.299) but moderate Spearman rank correlation (0.670).
contributions.domain: LLM inference efficiency / KV cache quantization
contributions.source_quote: Ablation studies validate that CA-derived masks outperform random masks by 6.67pp, confirming that quantization sensitivity is structurally determined by RoPE frequencies rather than randomly distributed.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Kitty (Xia et al., 2025) addresses this degradation through dynamic channel-wise precision boosting ... We observe that the channels requiring higher precision may not be dynamically varying outliers, but rather structurally determined by the rotary position embedding (RoPE) frequencies.
We leverage the Contextual Agreement (CA) metric from FASA (Wang et al., 2026) to identify structurally important RoPE frequency pairs.

Our work bridges frequency-aware analysis and quantization by using CA scores to identify channels requiring higher precision, replacing dynamic per-page selection with a static mask derived from structural importance.

notes: Grafts the CA metric from FASA (Wang et al., 2026) onto Kitty's (Xia et al., 2025) mixed-precision quantization framework, reusing Kitty's boost ratio, sink tokens and sliding window; the novelty is swapping dynamic magnitude selection for a static CA mask.
